title: Keep the analyzer working when source generation is suppressed

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.
continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
throw new InsufficientExecutionStackException($"This msgpack sequence has an object graph that exceeds the maximum depth allowed of {MaximumObjectGraphDepth}.");

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.intent: The analyzer must report its diagnostics for types that set SuppressSourceGeneration = true, as it did in version 3.1.0.

functional.text: The analyzer reports diagnostics for a [MessagePackObject] type with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
The analyzer behaves for such types as it did in version 3.1.0, before the regression in 3.1.1.

nonFunctional.text: The analyzer must not crash on invalid input in a suppressed type; it reports the problem instead. (inferred)
Types that do not suppress source generation keep their current diagnostics. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project with a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type that breaks a rule, such as a public member without a [Key] attribute, produces the matching MsgPack diagnostic in the build output.
The diagnostic appears in the IDE and in command-line builds even though the generator emits no formatter for that type.
Diagnostics point at the right location (member or type) in the suppressed type.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a suppressed [MessagePackObject] type that has a member missing [Key] expects the corresponding MsgPack diagnostic.
An analyzer test with a suppressed type that has duplicate or mixed key styles expects the matching diagnostic.

expectedBehaviours: For suppressed types, the set of diagnostic IDs, severities and locations matches what version 3.1.0 reported for the same source.
Rules that applied to suppressed types in 3.1.0 apply again. Rules that 3.1.0 skipped for suppressed types are not newly reported.
A suppressed type still gets no generated formatter, as in 3.1.0, and no formatter appears in the resolver.
expectedTests: A regression test reproducing the issue's sample source expects exactly the diagnostics that 3.1.0 produced.
A generator snapshot test confirms no formatter is emitted for a suppressed type while diagnostics are still reported.

expectedBehaviours: A suppressed type with invalid content, such as conflicting keys, unsupported member types or malformed attribute arguments, makes the analyzer report a diagnostic instead of throwing.
The build shows no AD0001 analyzer exception or generator crash warning (CS8785) for such input.
Diagnostics for other types in the same compilation are still reported when one suppressed type is invalid.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a suppressed type that has malformed or conflicting key attributes asserts the expected diagnostic and no analyzer exception diagnostic.
A test that runs the generator on invalid suppressed input asserts it finishes without exceptions.

expectedBehaviours: Types without SuppressSourceGeneration, or with it set to false, report the same diagnostics as before the change.
Generated formatter and resolver output for non-suppressed types does not change.
No new false positives appear for valid non-suppressed types.
expectedTests: The existing analyzer tests for non-suppressed types pass without changes.
The existing generator snapshot tests under Resources pass without changes to the expected files.

story.what: The change hardens TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo so that types with duplicate keys or mixed int/string keys no longer make the analyzer throw. Members whose key is already taken are no longer added to the intMembers and stringMembers dictionaries a second time. Members whose key kind does not match are skipped once DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys has been reported. The change also adds analyzer tests and execution tests for types with SuppressSourceGeneration = true, a README section on opting out of source generation, and changes the depth check in MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep from >= to >.
story.why: Issue 2234 reports that the analyzer stopped working for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types after 3.1.0. Before this change, a duplicate key reached Dictionary.Add, which throws on a key that is already present, and that exception stopped the analyzer. Now the analyzer reports the diagnostic and keeps going. The tests check which diagnostics suppressed types get, and that such types still serialize at run time without a generated formatter.

touches.note: Adds a member only if its key is not already in the dictionary, and skips members whose key kind does not match after reporting it. Applies to both the property loop and the field loop.
Depth check changed from >= to >, so the exception is thrown only when the depth is strictly above MaximumObjectGraphDepth.
New analyzer tests for the diagnostics reported, and not reported, on suppressed types, plus duplicate-key handling.
New execution tests: no generated formatter for a suppressed type, and a round trip through the dynamic resolver.
New docs section listing which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types.

findings.title: Analyzer entry point not changed; regression root cause unclear
findings.detail: The requirement is that the analyzer reports diagnostics for SuppressSourceGeneration = true types again, as it did in 3.1.0. The change only edits GetObjectInfo in TypeCollector: it guards the dictionary adds and skips members whose key kind does not match. It does not touch MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer or the way target types are chosen. GetObjectInfo already reported diagnostics before its early return for suppressed types. So the change does not show what broke in 3.1.1 or that it is fixed for suppressed types that have no duplicate or mixed keys. Nothing checks that the set of diagnostics (IDs, severities, locations) matches 3.1.0.

findings.title: A null string key on the first keyed field still throws
findings.detail: Say a type has no keyed properties and its first keyed field uses [Key(null)]. intKey and stringKey are both null. MsgPack002 (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull) is reported, and then searchFirst sets isIntKey to false. Execution reaches the field else-branch, where stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!) is called with null and throws ArgumentNullException. The property branch avoids this with 'else if (stringKey is not null)', but the field branch has no such guard. The analyzer therefore still fails with AD0001 on this invalid input, contrary to N1, in suppressed and non-suppressed types alike.

findings.title: Skipping mismatched-key members also skips checks on their types
findings.detail: The new 'continue' after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys exits the loop iteration before the recursive CollectCore(item.Type, item) call at the end. Diagnostics for the member's type, such as MsgPack003 when it is not a MessagePackObject, are therefore no longer reported for that member. This applies to all types, not only suppressed ones, so diagnostics for non-suppressed types drop out, which goes against N2. Once the key kind is fixed, the user gets new diagnostics they could have seen at the same time.

citations.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

findings.title: No tests for duplicate or mixed keys on fields
findings.detail: Hunks h5, h6 and h7 change the field path of GetObjectInfo: the mixed-key continue and the guarded intMembers and stringMembers adds. Every new analyzer test uses properties only, so none of them runs the field branch. The null-key crash in that branch went unnoticed for this reason.

findings.title: No generator test on invalid input or regression sample
findings.detail: The expectation asks for a test that runs the source generator on invalid suppressed input and checks that it finishes without exceptions (no CS8785). It also asks for a generator snapshot or regression test built from the issue's sample. The generator runs TypeCollector with reportDiagnostic set to null, and for non-suppressed types with duplicate keys it now quietly emits a formatter without the second member. None of the new tests covers the generator path; only the analyzer and run-time execution are tested.

refusals.reason: The change loosens the MaximumObjectGraphDepth check in MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep from >= to >, so untrusted payloads may nest one level deeper; that is a decision about handling untrusted input.
The change to the depth limit in the run-time deserializer cannot be traced to the analyzer requirement MP-2234.
The README adds documented behaviour stating which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types (MsgPack003, 004, 005, 012, 015) and which do not (MsgPack011, 016, 017).
